h.strategy: Measured interaction effects are dominated by a few robust regularities: an edit's effect is larger when the parent is weak overall and smaller when the parent is already strong (ceiling and floor); a component's removal costs less when another component already fills the same role; and an edit's effect changes most when the conditioning field controls the main bottleneck. Build each hypothesis on one of these, stated as a specific conditional. Prefer conditions that change overall parent quality substantially over conditions with subtle effects. Do not chase counterintuitive sign reversals. Spread hypotheses across different edited and conditioning fields, and use both HIGHER and LOWER directions roughly equally.

hyps.why: Replacing a missing direct input-output edge with a 3x3 conv adds a whole strong path, a larger gain than replacing an existing op.
Edge 0 feeds nodes 1 and 2 and the output, so adding a conv where there was none removes the main bottleneck.
Replacing a weak pooling op with a conv gives a bigger improvement than replacing an already-capable op.
Filling an empty edge with a learnable op gives a larger gain than modifying an existing op.
Removing a strong conv costs more accuracy than removing an average op (floor effect, a lower and more negative effect).
Deleting a conv on a main output edge hurts more than deleting a weak op.
Edge 4 takes its input from node 1, which is empty when edge 0 is none, so upgrading it is useless.
Edge 2 only reaches the output through edge 5, so a conv there is useless without it.
Adding a direct identity path to an empty edge gives a large gain from the gradient and information shortcut.
Upgrading a weak pooling op to a 3x3 conv gives a bigger gain than upgrading the average existing op.
